consistency_signals.detail: Main's "**Characterization theorem.**" (lower-case "theorem") is not matched by tools/proof_census.py (regex requires "**Theorem"), so the central equivalence has no LEDGER row; its supporting theorems (MAIN:T-finite-horizon-stochastic-reversible-unitary K3, MAIN:T-finite-horizon-process-dilation, MAIN:T-unavoidable-hidden-predictive-memory) do. Proof at papers/Main.md:608; the (ii)⟹(i) direction is imported under (T).

The theorem and book Lemma B.7.5 / Theorem B.7.5c are conditional on H-BG (global sign-aware classification). The kernel's unsigned premise BGIntegerClassification is refuted (GR:182, ROADMAP P2, ledger delta); kernel coverage is K1 (subresults only); the sign-aware replacement and its comparison with Bekir–Golomb are open. GR states this; the book Lemma B.7.5 states the phase-locking determination "up to the lemma's full gauge" under H-BG — check that every restatement (Main phase-locking, Appendix B) carries the open status, not only the hypothesis name.

consistency_signals.topic: Appendix B restatements that differ in scope or kind from the paper statement
consistency_signals.detail: B.2.5 states CP-indivisibility "of the substratum dynamics (under C1–C4)"; Main states it "for the permutation-dilation family" (Main status ledger: fails for general CPTP families). B.6.2 states 6 = 3⊕2⊕1 for "the internal components" without the H-link qualifier that SM Theorem 7 attaches to the physical reading. B.7.1 "Partition relativity" is a different statement from Main's Lemma of that name (the canonical-measure uniqueness claim). B.6b.1 is a Lemma with a narrower content than SM Theorem 7b (no Cabibbo-uniqueness clause); B.6.1 is a Proposition, SM 6 a Theorem.

consistency_signals.topic: Appendix A empirical-match cells vs SM/ch06 numbers
consistency_signals.detail: Row 6 Wolfenstein A "Within 1%" — SM/ch06 give 0.8165 vs 0.826 (1.2%, 0.8σ). Rows 13/N2 sin²θ13 "Within 1%" — SM/ch06/Juno give 0.02252 vs 0.02195±0.00056 (≈2.6%, 1.01σ). Row 21 m_b via Q_down "Within 1σ" — SM/ch06 give 4144 vs 4180±30 MeV (0.9%, i.e. 1.2σ by the quoted error). Row 1 1/α0 "Within ~0.5%" — ch06 §6.8 lists it as a structural input with no observed value; SM treats its native hypercharge reading as conditional on H-observer-bundle and H-Y-vertex.
Juno §5.1: "The formula for sin²θ₁₃ is fully derived"; Juno §6 and SM/appendix A classify it C (conditional on the emergent dressing of the Cabibbo identification).

SM:1317 compares sin²θ13 0.0225 with 0.0224 (0.4%) while SM:1276 uses 0.02195±0.00056 (1.01σ). SM:1316 lists A² = 0.6667 vs 0.683 as 1.2% (the A-level deviation; the A² deviation is ≈2.4%). SM:983-984 give m_e, m_μ at 1.2% (0.505, 104.4 MeV) beside SM:948-949 at 0.003%/0.002% — different constructions in different tables; labels should make the difference explicit.

ch06:190 gives m_μ = 105.74 MeV (0.08%) via "Koide closure with the structural m_e/m_τ = 1/(36π⁴)"; ch06 §6.8 (:305) and SM (:949, :1270) give 105.656 MeV (0.002%) from (Q, θ0; m_τ). Same chapter, two values; the SM counterpart table (:948) has only the second.

SM §7.6: 22 rows = 2 S + 5 C + 6 L + 3 R + 2 E + 3 M + 1 P (rows recounted). Appendix A A.4.1: 23 rows = 3 S + 7 C + 8 L + 1 M + 2 R + 2 E (recounted; matches its stated count) — explained in-text as broader than SM's table (adds 1/α0, A·B, MOND a0, neutrino rows). ch06:12 says §6.8 "collects the twenty-two predictions" but the §6.8 table has 24 rows with a different row set (adds 1/α0, δ0, A·B, θ̄, m_d, m_u; omits α1(M_Z), Q_down, m_b/m_τ, m_u/m_d). ch07:321 counts "the ten entries in this chapter's table" while appendix A, preface, ch08, ch09, ch18, ch19 count "eight gravitational-sector entries" — two different gravitational inventories. Headline "twenty-two SM observables, two S and five C" is uniform across SM, Substratum, Structure, the book and FULL (FULL mirrors every chapter verbatim).

Methodology §5.5 and §6.1 list determinism and bijectivity among the rungs that "follow as lemmas"; Methodology §4.4 and Main's posit ledger (iii) say the hidden-sector margin is closed with one empirical input, so bijectivity is part-empirical. The qualifier is present at the derivation and absent from the summary statements.
